subject: History
description: Akbar's reign, conquests, administration, religion, courtiers

questions.stem: AKBAR became Mughal emperor at the age of:

options.option_text: 15 years at the time of accession crown
18 years on coming of age formally crown

questions.explanation: AKBAR (1542-1605) — became emperor at AGE 13 in 1556, after father HUMAYUN's death (fell down library stairs). Coronation at KALANAUR (Punjab). BAIRAM KHAN was his regent for 4 years (1556-60); won SECOND BATTLE OF PANIPAT (1556) against Hemu (Hindu general of Adil Shah Suri) — re-established Mughal rule. Akbar took full charge of empire ~1560 (sent Bairam Khan to Mecca; later assassinated en route). Reigned 49 YEARS — one of longest in Indian history.
questions.subject: History

questions.explanation: Capital MOSTLY AGRA (built Agra Fort, 1565-73). FATEHPUR SIKRI (1571-85; ~14 years) — built to honour Sufi saint Sheikh Salim Chishti's blessing for a son (Salim, future Jahangir, born 1569). Beautiful Mughal-Rajput-Persian architecture: Buland Darwaza (entrance — tallest gateway in world, 54 m), Diwan-i-Khas (with central pillar — Akbar's throne), Panch Mahal, Salim Chishti's tomb, Jodha Bai's palace. Abandoned ~1585 (water shortage). LAHORE briefly capital 1585-1598 (during NW campaigns). Akbar died 1605 + buried at SIKANDRA (near Agra) in tomb he started + Jahangir completed.

questions.stem: Akbar's NINE GEMS (Navaratnas) included Birbal, Tansen, Abul Fazl, Faizi, Todar Mal + four others. Who was his FINANCE MINISTER?

options.option_text: Raja Todar Mal, the revenue master

questions.explanation: RAJA TODAR MAL — Akbar's revenue minister (Diwan-i-Ashraf). Devised the ZABTI / DAHSALA system: land surveyed, classified by fertility, average revenue based on PAST 10 YEARS' yield → fixed assessment. Standardised TAX RATES + units (BIGHA). Made Persian the official record-keeping language. Died 1589. NAVARATNAS (9 Gems): (1) Abul Fazl (court historian — Akbarnama, Ain-i-Akbari); (2) Faizi (poet, Abul Fazl's brother); (3) Tansen (legendary musician, Gwalior); (4) Birbal (Mahesh Das — wit, advisor; killed 1586); (5) Raja Todar Mal (finance); (6) Raja Man Singh (general, Amber); (7) Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana (poet, Bairam Khan's son); (8) Fakir Aziao-Din (advisor); (9) Mullah Do Piaza (jokester).

options.option_text: Sole worship of Allah, orthodox Islamic style
Eclectic synthesis of Hindu, Islam, Christian ideas
Conversion of Hindus to Islamic faith only
Strict caste segregation system enforced strongly

questions.explanation: DIN-I-ILAHI (1582) — Akbar's syncretic religious experiment. Drew from Islam, Hinduism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, Jainism. Emphasised: monotheism, ethical conduct, tolerance, reason. Few followers (~19; mostly courtiers) — never large movement. Ended with Akbar's death. SHOWCASED Akbar's tolerance: ABOLISHED JIZYA (poll-tax on non-Muslims, 1564); abolished pilgrimage tax (1563); allowed remarriage of widows; banned Sati (advised); MARRIED Rajput princess (Jodha Bai, mother of Jahangir); IBADAT KHANA (House of Worship, Fatehpur Sikri) — religious dialogue with all faiths. Issued MAHZAR-NAMA (1579) — declared Akbar arbiter on religious questions. (PYQ-favourite topic.)

A judicial system based on sharia

questions.explanation: MANSABDARI = Akbar's nobility + military rank system. MANSAB ('rank'). Each MANSABDAR had: (1) ZAT — personal rank, status + salary; (2) SAWAR — number of cavalry he must maintain. Ranks ranged 10 to 5000 (princes higher). Salary = JAGIR (assigned land revenue) or cash (from treasury). Built unified administrative + military hierarchy across diverse nobles (Turkish, Persian, Afghan, Indian Muslim, Rajput, etc.). Reduced fragmentation of medieval Iqta system. Continued under successors with modifications.

questions.stem: Major MILITARY conquests of Akbar included all EXCEPT:

options.option_text: Conquest of all of South India + Ceylon

questions.explanation: Akbar's empire stretched from Kabul to Bengal, Kashmir to North Deccan — but NOT South India / Ceylon. South Deccan still under Vijayanagara remnants + Bahmani sultanate offshoots (Ahmadnagar, Bijapur, Golkonda, Berar) — these were partly absorbed by his successors (Jahangir, Shah Jahan, Aurangzeb). RAJPUTS — most submitted via alliance (matrimonial — Akbar married Jodha Bai of Amber); MEWAR alone resisted (Maharana Pratap — Battle of HALDIGHATI 1576, indecisive; Pratap retreated). MAJOR CONQUESTS: Malwa (1561), Gondwana (1564 — defeated Rani Durgavati), Chittor (1568), Ranthambore (1569), GUJARAT (1572), BENGAL (1576), KABUL (1581 from half-brother), Kashmir (1586), Sind (1591), Berar (1596), KANDAHAR (1595).

questions.stem: ABUL FAZL, Akbar's court historian, wrote:
questions.explanation: ABUL FAZL — court historian, Akbar's confidant. Wrote: AKBARNAMA (3 vol; biography + history of Akbar's reign in Persian); AIN-I-AKBARI (vol 3 of Akbarnama; treatise on Akbar's administration, statistics, court customs, social life — invaluable historical source). Killed 1602 by Vir Singh Bundela (instigated by prince Salim/Jahangir, who saw Abul Fazl as obstacle). Distractor 1 = BABURNAMA by Babur himself (in Chagatai Turkish; auto-biography). Distractor 3 = JAHANGIRNAMA by Jahangir himself. Distractor 4 = PADSHAHNAMA by Abdul Hamid Lahori (under Shah Jahan).
